name: navigator-scan-permission
body:
The distributed `codebase-navigator` agent prompt (`opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, product source embedded into the apg binary via `include_str!` and installed by `apg init` into `~/.opencode/agents/`) must stop holding a bespoke scan-consent ritual and instead delegate scan authorization to opencode's per-call tool permission. The frontmatter grant changes from `apg_scan: allow` to `apg_scan: ask`, so opencode itself prompts the user whenever `apg_scan` is called; the user may choose "always allow" to suppress future prompts. The prompt keeps its don't-guess-at-a-dead-graph / don't-re-scan-silently intent but drops every separate consent step, because the permission layer is now the gate.

Surfaces this change-set edits:
- `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` (File, `docs`, 623 lines) — frontmatter `apg_scan: allow` → `apg_scan: ask`; non-negotiable rule 7's "ask the user first (via the `question` tool) … Only run `apg_scan` after they approve" restated as "when the graph is missing/stale, run `apg_scan` (the permission is `ask`, so opencode prompts the user) — never paper over a dead graph with guesses"; the query-patterns "ask the user first — scans can be lengthy on large codebases" row dropped; the "### Scanning a project" intro's "ask the user before running a scan … never kick one off unprompted" dropped; the "gate for every answer" bullet's "Ask the user first (via the `question` tool)" dropped; the "When a scan is needed" step 0 deleted and step 1 becomes the run step; the Implementation-flow "you run scans (after user approval)" and cadence step 3 "(after user approval)" drop the approval clause, the `ask` prompt being the approval.
- `tests/main_e2e.rs` — extend the EXISTING coherence test `rust.main_e2e.e2e.coordinator_agent_carries_review_action_and_dispatch_prose` (function, `test`, lines ~2148-2266) to also assert the navigator frontmatter grants `apg_scan: ask` (and `apg_scan: allow` is absent) plus the absence of the removed scan-consent prose; update its doc comment to say it pins the navigator's permission grants (review-action + scan) and the dispatch/isolation protocol; leave the fn name unchanged.

Acceptance criteria (all observable in the prompt / test):
1. The navigator frontmatter grants `apg_scan: ask`, not `apg_scan: allow`.
2. No scan-consent ritual remains: no "ask the user first" / "get explicit approval before starting one" / "ask the user before running a scan" / "(after user approval)" wording for scans, and no `question`-tool scan-consent step.
3. The stale-graph guidance still tells the agent to run `apg_scan` rather than guess, now with the `ask` permission supplying the prompt.
4. The coherence test asserts `apg_scan: ask` and the absence of the old consent prose.
5. Scope: product-source prompt + the existing coherence test only; no binary behaviour change; no other `opencode-suite/agents/*` file edited; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts and are never edited.
